request.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE pixel-art tactical dungeon scene. Image 1 is the NEW STYLE reference: very small economical sprites, thick dark pixel outlines, tiny orange/gold helmets, charcoal clothing, grey simple weapons, low-detail muted green square stone, tiny warm torchlight accents. Stay as simple and low-resolution-looking as this reference; no realistic anatomy, no detailed armor, no microtexture. Image 2 is ONLY our FLOOR PROJECTION reference: copy the steep diamond angles of its large field (tile top width:height 4:3, edge rise 3 for run4). Do not use the reference1 top-down FLOOR camera. Scene: A small square guardroom with one closed chest at the back and two wall torches. Four guards stand on four well-separated cells. Quiet green square stone floor, low back walls only.. Characters: four small orange-helmet dungeon guards, with a short sword+shield, a small axe, a compact crossbow, and another plain shield. Chunky compact silhouettes, arms and boots clearly separate, short garments, no hanging trinkets; animation-friendly stable color blocks. Each character's feet stand directly inside ONE clearly identifiable floor tile, centered with generous space to every tile seam. Each sprite is modest in scale relative to a tile. Flat connected floor only, NO circular discs, NO plinths, NO raised single tile under feet, NO display stands. Characters MUST use the same front three-quarter ISOMETRIC angle as the floor camera, looking down enough to see helmet tops and shoulders. ALL four face toward screen LOWER RIGHT, faces visible; no rear views, no mixed facings. Square canvas, entire room visible with margins, dark neutral charcoal background, calm floor colors. Few large color clusters per object, hard pixel edges, no blur, no smooth 3D gradients, no particle effects, no motion blur, no glowing weapons. No UI, no text, no watermark, no labels. These are fresh designs in the reference's visual language.
